children.value: > Fact From Story Google’s recent advances in AI-based search were implemented with “the goal of discouraging end-users from visiting the websites of Class members who are part of the digital news and publishing line of commerce.”
> > Fact From Story SGE offers web searchers a way to seek information in a conversational mode, but ultimately keeps users in Google’s “walled garden” as it “plagiarizes” their content.
> > > Fact From Story Publishers also can’t block SGE
> > > Commonsense Knowledge If news publishers can't block SGE, then Google will continue to discourage end-users from visiting the websites of news publishers.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Keeping users within a "walled garden" discourages them from visiting external websites.
> Fact From Story AI technologies like Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot are worsening the problem.

> > Fact From Story The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Siphoning off news publishers’ content, readers, and ad revenue is a problem for the news publishers.
> Commonsense Knowledge Discouraging end-users from visiting websites of news publishers worsens the problem for the news publishers.
